text:
rachel: FYI observability caught repeated cross-az latency ripples from rack r-9 this morning. p50 fine, but p99 spikes ~2s every 20m. looks correlated with a large model warmup job.

devin: which tenant / job id?

rachel: tenant t-8246, job warmup-2026-03-21-01. It runs large prefill sequences to prime KV + CUDA caches. stack traces show repeated pci-e resets and MIG remapping on host (nvlink reported as flapping).

juan: oof. warmups with large sequence lengths can cause KV churn and GPU page pin churn. if MIG slices are being remapped we might be hitting driver/device reprobe storms. any kernel logs?

rachel: attaching excerpt: 
```
Mar 21 01:12:02 host-009 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 21 01:12:03 host-009 kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: type 0x04
Mar 21 01:12:03 host-009 nvidia: MIG: remapping slice 2 -> 0 due to allocation failure
```

erin: That pattern explains the p99 ripples. If a slice remap happens, other tenants on same card see stutter.

devin: mitigation options: 1) soft-move t-8246 to a fractional dedicated pool during their window (they run predictable warmups 01:00-02:00 UTC), 2) enforce a warmup-rate limiter (allow warmup-kv ops/sec), 3) require them to use dedicated prefill nodes (new infra).

juan: fractional dedicated is fastest. ops cost calc: moving them to a fractional slice increases monthly cost by ~6% for that rack's billing bucket; but reduces incident impact across multiple tenants.

rachel: can we instead set a conservative MIG carveout policy: reserve slice 0 on each card for system/other tenants, and limit hot-remap attempts to 1 per 5m?

erin: kernel/driver changes are risky and slow to roll. Ops prefers policy-level fix first.

ops-bot: NOTE created ticket-6030: "t-8246 warmup-induced pci-e remap -> cross-tenant p99 spikes" assigned to eng-infra.

devin: Proposal: schedule a fractional-dedicated move for t-8246 weekdays 01:00-02:30 UTC for 2 weeks, while model-team optimizes warmup to batch prefill. Ops to apply network/egress policer to limit concurrent prefill RPCs in the interim.

rachel: i'll run a cost simulation and post numbers. quick calc: extra fractional slice consumes 0.08 rack-equivalent hours per warmup window -> est $1.2k/month. cheaper than SLA penalties.

juan: also add a telemetry probe: detect MIG remap events per-GPU and auto-evacuate non-critical tenants from affected GPU until stability window passes. That avoids manual mitigation.

erin: agree. short-term action items: 1) ops apply policer 2) infra schedule fractional-dedicated carveout 3) model-team A/B test coalesced prefill.

rachel: ops - please apply policer and create a canary to validate no regressions.

ops-bot: ACTION ops.apply-policer t-8246 rate=200rps burst=50 duration=1h -> success (applied to rack r-9).

devin: i'll book time with model-team to discuss prefill changes. will open follow-up RFC for adaptive warmup backpressure.

rachel: thanks everyone. i'll update ticket-6030 with the fractional carveout schedule and close the loop after 48h monitoring. :white_check_mark:
